evals.prompt: We have three Linear initiatives named MVP, Growth, and Advanced, twelve projects, and about 160 mixed tickets. The initiatives are broad and never really finish. Set up a durable delivery structure without modifying Linear yet. Explain how you would classify the existing records and show the default hierarchy and canonical-source split.
evals.expected_output: A read-only migration proposal using horizons, bounded outcome plans, vertical features, and task detail; it preserves provider provenance, avoids one-ticket-per-feature import, and assigns field-level canonical ownership.
expectations: The response uses Horizon -> Outcome plan -> Vertical feature -> Task as the default hierarchy.
The response classifies provider entities by meaning rather than retaining names such as initiative or project mechanically.
The response explicitly avoids mutating Linear before authorization and rejects automatic one-ticket-per-feature import.
The response separates portfolio priority authority from Git-owned executable scope, dependencies, evidence, and rollout.

evals.prompt: $delivery next. PLAN-CHECKOUT is proposed/approved but has no owner and portfolio priority has not been reconciled. CHK-01 is not_started/approved, has no dependencies, and has an assigned feature owner. Start implementing it now.
evals.expected_output: The assistant refuses to start writes, evaluates the explicit next-eligibility predicate, and reports the first actionable plan-level gate without silently changing state.
expectations: The response does not begin implementation or silently activate the plan.
The response identifies that the containing plan is not active and also recognizes missing plan ownership or priority reconciliation as eligibility gates.
The response keeps planning approval distinct from delivery status.
The response gives a concrete state-transition sequence that would make the feature eligible.

evals.prompt: Plan a shared-expense ledger. After the atomic expense feature, timeline, settlements, and active-context capture look parallel. Timeline must display settlement and reversal events, and two branches may touch migrations and shared command types. I want maximum parallelism but no risky merges. Define the DAG, WIP rule, and what must be frozen before execution.
evals.expected_output: A dependency-aware feature DAG that owns the shared event contract upstream, treats parallel relations as candidates, limits WIP, and requires an approved contract-freeze record with physical ownership and QA gates.
expectations: The response prevents timeline and settlement from running as independent siblings unless the settlement/event contract is owned and frozen upstream.
The response treats parallelizable_with as candidate compatibility rather than authorization.
The response requires an approved current freeze record with exact schemas/signatures or DDL, file/function ownership, merge order, and independent QA.

The response uses the repository WIP policy or, when none exists, defaults to two active features per plan (one critical-path and one independent), counts review as WIP, and falls back to serial execution when freeze conditions are not satisfied.

evals.prompt: $delivery next. The handoff points to PAY-02, which is in_progress/approved and owned by this execution. Its plan is active/approved, priority is reconciled, dependencies are completed, and its physical boundary is assigned. The two-slot WIP limit is full: PAY-02 occupies one slot and another independent feature occupies the other. Their approved contract freeze is current. Resume PAY-02 after the session interruption.
evals.expected_output: The assistant resumes the owned feature after rechecking continuation gates, counts its existing WIP slot once, and does not apply the new-work not_started predicate or start another feature.
expectations: The response distinguishes resuming owned in_progress work from selecting a new not_started feature.
The response rechecks approval, plan activation, dependencies, ownership, and applicable parallel-safety gates.
The response counts the existing WIP slot once and does not reject continuation merely because no new slot is available.
The response does not reset delivery status, silently transfer ownership, or start another feature.

evals.prompt: $delivery next. UI-03 is approved and eligible, and I authorize its new feature task using gpt-5.6-sol with medium effort. Its feature recommends the same pair. The host defaults to gpt-6-astra/high; create_thread supports model and thinking, and both requested values are available. Dispatch UI-03, then show the execution checkpoint.
evals.expected_output: An explicit Sol Medium dispatch and an accurate checkpoint, without inheriting Astra High or treating feature metadata as configuration.
expectations: The create_thread call explicitly contains model gpt-5.6-sol and thinking medium.
The checkpoint distinguishes the requested pair and host confirmation/readback evidence.
The assistant neither changes the feature to match host defaults nor raises effort because the task is UI work.

evals.prompt: Resume an approved feature whose user-selected settings are gpt-5.6-sol/medium. The existing task reports gpt-6-astra/high, and the host cannot change either setting. No fallback is authorized. The old checkpoint says inherited; keep working from it.
evals.expected_output: The assistant preserves existing work, identifies the unresolved settings mismatch, and seeks the missing configuration decision before dependent implementation while continuing independent preparation.
expectations: The assistant does not treat inherited or host limitation as satisfaction of the execution gate.
The assistant does not silently authorize Astra High or discard completed work.
The assistant surfaces the specific mismatch and limits its question to the missing setting/fallback authorization.
